title: Himachal Pradesh HC: Burden Shifts to Employer Once Reinstated Workman Pleads He Stayed Unemployed
case_name: Chattar Singh v. Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board Ltd.
card_summary: A Labour Court had reinstated a daily-wage workman but refused him back wages, and he challenged the denial. The High Court held that once a reinstated workman pleads he remained unemployed after termination, the burden shifts to the employer to prove he was gainfully employed elsewhere. HPSEBL having failed to discharge that burden, the Court ordered 50% back wages with interest within six weeks.
card_tip: A bare denial that a reinstated workman is owed back wages will not hold up; an employer must lead evidence of the workman's gainful employment elsewhere, not just assert it.
verification_notes: The case number CWP No. 8209 of 2025, the 16 September 2026 decision date, Justice Sandeep Sharma's bench, the underlying award in Reference No. 141 of 2004, the burden-shifting holding, and the 50% back wages with interest direction are consistent across LiveLaw's and Courtbook's reports.
